references.text: Moses prophesied that the Lord would scatter Israel among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other – a warning of exile and captivity among the nations, as Jesus describes in [ref:5 Mos 28:64|Deuteronomy 28:64].

The prophecy that a people from far away will come and besiege all the cities of the land and destroy them with the sword. [ref:5 Mos 28:49-52|Deuteronomy 28:49-52] points forward to the destruction Jesus warns about.
Isaiah laments that enemies have trampled God's sanctuary, which corresponds to the image of Jerusalem being "trampled by Gentile nations" in [ref:Jes 63:18|Isaiah 63:18].

Daniel's vision of the sanctuary being trampled for a set time until it is restored. [ref:Dan 8:13-14|Daniel 8:13-14] reflects Jesus' words that Jerusalem will be trampled until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
Daniel prophesies about the destruction of the city and the sanctuary, which directly connects to Jesus' prophecy concerning the fall of Jerusalem in [ref:Dan 9:26-27|Daniel 9:26-27].
Daniel's prophecy about a set time when the power of God's holy people will be broken corresponds with the idea of "the times of the Gentiles" that must be fulfilled, cf. [ref:Dan 12:7|Daniel 12:7].
Zechariah prophesies that Jerusalem will become a heavy stone for all peoples – a parallel to Jesus' words that Gentile nations will trample Jerusalem, cf. [ref:Sak 12:3|Zechariah 12:3].
Lamentations describes how the Lord has trodden Judah's virgin in the winepress, an image of Jerusalem being trampled, cf. [ref:Klag 1:15|Lamentations 1:15].

John sees in his vision that the holy city will be trampled by Gentile nations for forty-two months – a clear parallel to Jesus' words that Jerusalem will be trampled until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled, [ref:Åp 11:2|Revelation 11:2].

Paul speaks about how hardening has come upon part of Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in. "The times of the Gentiles" in Luke and "the fullness of the Gentiles" in [ref:Rom 11:25|Romans 11:25] both point to a set time for the role of the Gentiles in salvation history.
Ezekiel speaks about a day drawing near, the Lord's day, a dark time for the nations – a parallel to the appointed times for the Gentiles, cf. [ref:Esek 30:3|Ezekiel 30:3].
The immediate context where Jesus speaks of Jerusalem's siege and destruction as a fulfillment of prophecies, [ref:Luk 21:20-22|Luke 21:20-22].
